name: Berkshire Hathaway
headline: A conglomerate led by low-cost auto insurance and a railroad, backed by $359 billion in cash and Treasury bills.
what_short: Insurance, railroad, utilities and many businesses
what_it_does: Berkshire Hathaway owns GEICO and other insurers, the BNSF railroad, the BHE group of utilities, and a wide range of manufacturing, service and retail businesses. It also holds a large portfolio of listed shares. Insurance premiums paid in advance give it money to invest before claims are paid.
why_it_passed: GEICO, the low-cost auto insurer, kept its combined ratio (claims plus costs as a share of premiums) at 84.7% in 2025, a level that means an underwriting profit.
Its manufacturing, service and retail businesses earn roughly 12% to 15% a year before tax on the tangible capital they use, and BNSF earns about 12%.
The group holds $359.2 billion of cash and Treasury bills, up from $113.0 billion in 2017, and its parent company debt is only $20.4 billion.
The analysis found no path to ruin for the whole group, and management's integrity passed.
why_not_now: The analysis values the shares at $316 to $347 against a price of $504.75, which is about 45% above the top of that range. At that price the expected return is below the roughly 10% the analysis requires, and the return implied for one of the group's parts (2.5%) is below the 5.63% a 30-year US Treasury bond pays.
watch: BHE, the utility group, earns only about 4% to 5% on its capital, carries heavy debt, and has an unquantified wildfire liability.
The group's cash is growing faster than the businesses that can use it, and the cash earns only about the Treasury bill rate.
The five largest share holdings make up 66% of the $323.8 billion portfolio, so a fall in a few stocks would matter.
